burnovers_TN2252_Table30_p125-126_PDF163: Jordan Hill Rd / Granite Hill Rd

H01.claim: TN 2135 identified 19 burnovers; TN 2252 lists 23 (#20–23 added after TN 2135 during rescue-data analysis, Sec. 10 / App. F)

H02.claim: Severity split from tables: TN2252 Table 30 = 14 Cat1 (1,20,3,4,5,6,7,8,21,13,22,15,17,19) + 9 Cat2 (2,9,10,11,12,23,14,16,18). TN2252 text p.123 says 'fourteen ... Category 1 ... and seven ... Category 2' (sums to 21). TN2135 text p.117 says eleven Cat1 and seven Cat2 (=18 of 19); its Table 33 (p.119/PDF 149) gives 11 Cat1 + 8 Cat2.

H03.claim: Before 10:00 Nov 8, Table 30 lists 11 burnovers (#1,2,20,3,4,5,6,7,8,21,9) = 9 Cat1 + 2 Cat2; TN2252 text p.123 repeats TN2135's 'nine ... seven Category 1, two Category 2' (true only for the original 19). TN2252 p.137 also says 10 burnovers by 09:35 in Concow+Paradise.
H03.scoring_note: 2026-10-24 threshold review: H03 is conditional - only scored if the deck states a pre-10:00/morning burnover count; H02 split is now required by the instruction (Section 4 sentence).

H04.claim: Table 39: Total 352 min / 569 max is a person×exposure count; unique individuals 261 min / 416 max. 261 = 70 Concow + 191 Paradise.

H05.claim: 8 high-urgency-of-formation TRAs with civilians (A,B,C,E,G,H,I,J); 6 had high peak hazard (A,B,C,H,I,J); E and G were moderate (▲▲). TF-TRA 7 says 'High hazard conditions impacted at least 261 civilians in eight TRAs'.

H06.claim: Table 11: Zone 6 first fire 07:57 (before 08:01 request), Zone 4 first fire 08:41. Text p.61 says 'Zone 4 was the only zone in which fire had already started, with the first fire observation at 07:57'.

H07.claim: TN2252 p.60: 'first observation of fire directly by firefighters in the Concow zone occurred by an engine on Rim Road at 07:32'; p.63: 'first in-person observation of fire in Concow by first responders was at 07:20'. TN2135 p.122: 'Firsthand observations on Rim Road at 07:20 on November 8'.

H08.claim: Zones 3/8: order request 07:46 is 4/3 min before first fire 07:50/07:49 (Table 11 Δ 00:04/00:03); CodeRED 07:57 is 7/8 min after first fire (derived; not printed as such). Text p.58: order 'three minutes ahead of the fire's arrival in Zone 8'; CodeRED 07:57 'the quickest CodeRED implementation of the day'.

H09.claim: Table 30 footnote d: traffic gridlocked/obstructed before fire arrival at #4 Skyway(upper), #6 Pentz, #7 Pearson, #8 Bille, #22 Neal. p.59: 'The impact of the delayed notifications on the other zones is beyond the scope of this study and would be difficult to quantify' (also for zones without reverse-911 calls). Unsupported: 'earlier orders would have prevented burnovers/deaths', any lives-saved number.

H10.claim: Table 4 (p.28): Paradise 927, Magalia 1264, Concow 164 OHU/egress lane; ratio 'not an explicit measure of road capacity'. Table 5 (p.32): Zones 3,8,14 = 316; Zones 10,11,Lower Neal = 278; Valley View/Ridge = 187. Table 6 (p.33): merging south of Paradise 2950 or 2529; Paradise used 1588; Magalia 2527. 'The values in Tables 4 through 6 do not include any reductions of lanes caused by fire or obstructions.' Supported counterfactual-type statement p.93 (Clark Rd backup): 'Had the backup extended further, or had the fire advanced faster, additional civilian exposure to fire would have occurred.'

H11.claim: TN2135 p.140: initial high ember flux zone reached 1 km (0.6 mi) into Paradise; significant spot fires to 3.4 km (2.1 mi); 'extensive fuel treatments reaching hundreds of meters from the community would be required ... very significant environmental and financial impacts ... difficult to initially implement and subsequently maintain'. p.136: effectiveness of fuel treatments 'beyond the scope of this report'.

H12.claim: Table 30 footnote e / Table 12 footnote a: #20 Camelot 07:55 and #5 Windermere 08:35 (and #14 13:10) are earliest available observations; burnover conditions existed before; Table 12 intervals for #20/#5 (1:10/0:18, 1:50/0:58) are therefore bounds.

H14.claim: TN2135 p.122: shortly before 08:00 spot fires east of Pentz Rd; by 08:30 main front reached Paradise Apple View Way–Merrill Rd 1 km; a little over 70 min later 2.8 km (1.9 mi) front. TN2252 Table 11: first fire Zone 8 07:49, Zone 3 07:50. TN2252 p.158: fire front hit Paradise ~08:30.

traps.T01: TN2135 appendix technical-discussion comments (e.g., TD-076 'even with hours of notice, there still would have been casualties') are interviewee statements, not NIST findings (TN2135 PDF 403).
traps.T02: Wind-vs-fire-induced-wind driver of front arrival in Paradise 'not possible to determine' (TN2135 p.122) — claiming a definitive driver is unsupported.
